newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: GOLF-DEFENDING CHAMPION MCNULTY PULLS OUT OF DUTCH OPEN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-DEFENDING CHAMPION MCNULTY PULLS OUT OF DUTCH OPEN.

text.p: Defending champion Mark McNulty was forced to retire from the Dutch Open on Friday after aggravating a back injury.

The 43-year-old Zimbabwean, who suffers perennial back problems, may now turn to an alternative medicine man banned from the Royal and Ancient Golf Club's premises last week at the British Open, in a desperate attempt to overcome his injury.

McNulty has for years had a middle back problem, which has caused him to alter his swing and shorten his driving. But the problem had spread to his lower lumber region by the time he started the second round only five strokes off the Dutch Open lead after an opening two-under-par 69.
Having suffered acute discomfort on the practice range, McNulty soldiered on for six holes but then had to pull out of the event.
"The problem flared up again last week in the British Open," said McNulty, who picked up his biggest cheque for some time when he tied for 32nd at Royal Troon.
"But this week the pain spread to my lower back as well and I knew there would be a chance I'd have to pull out today the moment I hit my first shot.
"I tried to keep it going but I was worried I was doing myself further damage by playing on."

The Zimbabwean, who took his 15th European Tour victory in a 19-year career when he won the Dutch title last year, had intensive treatment from the touring physiotherapy wagon after walking from the course.
But he may also try a more controversial route by seeking help from the former caddie who has turned to alternative medicine, the American chiropractor who goes only by the name of 'Doc'.

He was the man ejected from official British Open premises last week when treating Severiano Ballesteros. 'Doc' says he relies on a 'space research instrument that gives soundwaves through the body' and is at Hilversum where he is treating several players, including McNulty's fellow Zimbabwean Tony Johnstone.

"I've reached the point where I'll try anything," said McNulty. "I know you have to be careful so I'll be investigating this man thoroughly. But I think I know the technique he uses and it's tried and tested, so it may help me."
